R0051.title: Application Reverse Engineering
R0051.definition: Restoring an application's source code or runtime logic through reverse engineering.
R0051.description: For web applications, WeChat mini-programs, and Android apps, source code can be directly or easily restored, exposing all application processing logic. For iOS apps, reverse analysis can be performed using tools such as class-dump, Hopper, and IDA. When security policies are implemented on the client side, there is a risk of them being cracked or bypassed.
R0051.influence: May cause security processes within the application to be broken and data to be forged.

observables: Analysis behavior signatures of tools such as class-dump and IDA appear even after the app has been hardened
Plaintext security logic with stripped obfuscation or restored form appears in the client code
A large volume of reverse-engineering-based automated script invocations appears for the same app version within a short window
Source code packages of mini-programs or web applications are pulled at high frequency by external IPs
Runtime logs indicate that app security policies such as signature verification and root detection have been bypassed

R0051-001.title: Application Traffic Interception
R0051-001.definition: Restoring an application's request structure and monitoring response data through packet capture.
R0051-001.description: Packet capture involves intercepting, replaying, editing, and saving data packets sent and received over the network. Through packet capture, an application's request methods and structure can be analyzed to enable business logic reconstruction, simulation, and process automation as a substitute for the client (R0001).
R0051-001.influence: May cause security processes within the application to be broken and data to be forged.

references.title: MASTG-TEST-0244: Missing Certificate Pinning in Network Traffic - OWASP

observables: Application network traffic exhibits certificate signatures of man-in-the-middle proxies or packet capture tools
Client requests are detected carrying proxy identifiers from packet capture tools such as Charles, Fiddler, and mitmproxy
The same endpoint is scraped at high frequency by external tools, with request timing exhibiting scripted replay characteristics
Certificate pinning fails and decrypted HTTPS traffic reveals request structures from non-official clients
Request headers contain debug fields injected by packet capture tools or anomalous proxy routing information

R0051-002.title: HTTP Request Analysis
R0051-002.definition: Restoring an application's request structure and monitoring response data through packet capture.
R0051-002.description: For applications that transmit data using text-based protocols such as HTTP/HTTPS, a man-in-the-middle can be used to capture sent and received data, thereby reconstructing the application's execution logic to enable automated operations.
R0051-002.influence: May cause security processes within the application to be broken and data to be forged.

observables: After HTTP/HTTPS endpoints are intercepted via man-in-the-middle, structured requests from non-official clients appear
Request parameter ordering, signature algorithms, or field naming exhibit scripted characteristics of reverse-engineered reconstruction
High-frequency requests to the same endpoint originate from non-official clients with highly regular request structures
Session tokens or signatures in requests are bulk-replayed, with timing exhibiting automation characteristics
Endpoint call frequency and parameter combinations concentrate abnormally within a short window, deviating from normal user behavior
